claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and ascetic who lived from approximately 185 to 253 CE.
Origen was born at Alexandria of Christian parents and became head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, first informally and then officially in 203 CE.
Origen wrote two books on the resurrection.
The work On the Resurrection survives only in fragments.
In On the Resurrection, Origen discussed the story of Lazarus and the rich man, addressing questions about whether souls have bodies after death and before the resurrection.
Origen argued that those who attain the resurrection will be like angels, without flesh, based on the Sadducees' challenge to Jesus.
Origen's treatise On First Principles refers back to his other works on the resurrection, indicating he had discussed the topic at greater length elsewhere.
Origen was one of the most influential and controversial figures in early Christian theology, and has been described as the greatest genius the early church ever produced.
